history.dynasty: Pallava (initial structure, 5th century, per tradition); Chola (11th-12th century - outer temple; Rajendra Chola I, Rajaraja Chola I, Kulottunga I/III); Vijayanagara (Krishnadevaraya, 1516 - 120-ft gopuram and 100-pillared hall)
history.period: 5th-16th century CE (tradition; present complex largely 11th-16th century)
history.summary: One of the most important Shiva temples in South India and the Vayu (air) sthalam among the Pancha Bhoota Sthalams. The swayambhu white lingam - said to resemble an elephant's trunk and untouched by human hands - is worshipped as Kalahasteeswara; the complex includes a separate shrine of Gnana Prasunambika and sub-shrines for Kasi Viswanatha, Annapurna, Suryanarayana and Subramanya (see row 1234). Its name comes from the sthala purana of the spider (Sri), snake (Kala) and elephant (Hasti) that worshipped Shiva here and attained moksha; Kannappa's offering of his eyes is also set here. Also known as the Rahu-Ketu kshetra and Dakshina Kasi/Dakshin Kailash; the ghee lamps inside the sanctum are said to flicker as if moved by air. District noted as Tirupati (created 2022); older sources give Chittoor.

name: Sri Kalahasteeswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Srikalahasti, in Tirupati district on the banks of the Swarnamukhi river about 36 km from Tirupati, is an ancient temple town known as the 'Kashi of the South' (Dakshina Kasi). It is famed as a Rahu-Ketu remedial pilgrimage centre and for its hand-crafted Srikalahasti Kalamkari art.
